title: Post hoc neural gait analysis detects a tandem-walk metric difference in an ataxia trial
summary: A deep pose-estimation pipeline extracted gait measurements from a small convenience subset of a randomized ataxia trial. Post hoc analysis found a tandem-walk metric difference between troriluzole and placebo, while the natural-walk comparison was nonsignificant and treatment did not reduce falls. The result supports a bounded retrospective measurement finding, without confirmatory evidence of clinical benefit.
ai_technology: MPII-trained multi-stage deep neural network for human pose estimation; derived Pose Dispersion Index
organization: Yale School of Medicine; Biohaven Pharmaceuticals; Massachusetts General Hospital; UCLA School of Medicine

evidence.tested: Among 218 randomized participants, interpretable paired videos were available for 67 tandem-walk and 56 natural-walk participants. The pretrained deep network tracked body keypoints used to calculate pose dispersion. An adjusted treatment-by-visit mixed model reported a week 48 tandem-walk coefficient 0.584, 95% CI 0.137–1.031, p=0.010. The natural-walk difference was nonsignificant, and the source explicitly reports no treatment effect on falls.
evidence.unknown: The video endpoint was post hoc and was not the original recording purpose. Convenience and quality selection retained only 30.7% and 25.7% of participants, respectively, introducing selection and measurement limitations. Only baseline/final recordings were analyzed, supplementary metric implementation was not independently reconstructed, and the finding does not establish prespecified efficacy, reduced falls or clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: The learned pose model extracted body coordinates from trial videos, enabling a source-specific gait metric and treatment-group comparison that standard clinician ratings did not directly provide. Trial randomization does not make this later AI-derived endpoint a locked prospective evaluation.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary trial/video eligibility, pretrained pose-model and derived-index Methods, post hoc mixed/Poisson evaluation, tandem/natural-walk Results, no-falls-benefit statement and convenience-video limitations. Supplementary metric implementation not independently reconstructed. No prospective locking or clinical-benefit claim adopted. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.
